title: An acknowledged write survives kill -9
notes: The adapter drives the server through PDB_CONF_CONTROL (an executable): `$PDB_CONF_CONTROL kill9` sends SIGKILL to the server and waits for it to exit; `$PDB_CONF_CONTROL restart` starts it again on the same ports and data directory and returns once the native port answers. Both exit non-zero on failure.
Modes: groupsync is the shipped default and MUST hold these cases (an acked commit has been fsynced by the group); sync must too. nosync is never in a durability lane.

steps: CREATE TABLE conf_dur1 (id int8 PRIMARY KEY, v text).
Insert ids 1..500 one autocommit statement at a time, recording each id whose execute RETURNED successfully.
cases.expected: Every acked id is present (a superset is allowed only for an id whose execute was in flight at the kill; this case kills after all returned, so exactly 1..500).

cases.purpose: An acked multi-statement COMMIT survives kill -9 atomically.
steps: Autocommit OFF; INSERT 100 rows into conf_dur2; UPDATE one of them; COMMIT (acked).
cases.expected: All 100 rows with the update applied.

steps: Batch-insert 1000 rows into conf_dur3 (one SDK batch call, acked).

cases.purpose: An acked KV SET (native frame where the SDK has one) survives kill -9, visible over the SDK and RESP after restart.
steps: SDK kv set conf:dur4 = 'durable'; SDK incr conf:dur4n three times (acked).
SDK get conf:dur4; RESP GET conf:dur4n.

cases.purpose: Connection loss is reported, not hung or silently retried, and a new connection works after restart.
steps: On A run SELECT 1: expect an error within 10 s whose SQLSTATE is class 08 (connection exception).
restart; open B; SELECT 1. If the SDK has a pool/reconnect facility, a fresh borrow also works.
cases.expected: A errors with 08xxx promptly; B returns 1.
